body:
### Problem

LSP diagnostics are not displayed in unnamed (`[No Name]`) buffers, even when a language server publishes diagnostics for the exact URI Neovim sent in `textDocument/didOpen`.

On Linux, `vim.uri_from_bufnr()` returns `file://` for every unnamed buffer. `vim.uri_to_fname('file://')` then returns `/`, so the built-in diagnostics handler assigns the diagnostics to a different buffer named `/` instead of the original unnamed buffer. Multiple unnamed buffers also share the same document URI.

This is about buffers with an empty name, not merely named files that have not been written to disk yet.

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim --clean -u minimal_init.lua`

Save the following as `minimal_init.lua`, then run:

```sh
nvim --clean --headless -i NONE -u minimal_init.lua
```

This is a self-contained in-process test server using the supported function form of `cmd`. It goes through `vim.lsp.start()`, initialization, `textDocument/didOpen`, and the client's notification dispatcher. The server publishes one diagnostic for the URI it receives. No plugins or external language server are required.

```lua
local original = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
local second = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(true, false)
vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(original, 0, -1, false, { 'example' })
vim.bo[original].filetype = 'text'

-- An in-process test server: publish one diagnostic for the URI received in didOpen.
local client_id = vim.lsp.start({
  name = 'unnamed-diagnostic-repro',
  cmd = function(dispatchers)
    local closing, request_id = false, 0
    return {
      request = function(method, _, callback)
        request_id = request_id + 1
        local id = request_id
        vim.schedule(function()
          callback(nil, method == 'initialize' and {
            capabilities = { textDocumentSync = { openClose = true, change = 1 } },
          } or nil, id)
        end)
        return true, id
      end,
      notify = function(method, params)
        if method == 'textDocument/didOpen' then
          vim.schedule(function()
            local uri = params.textDocument.uri
            print('didOpen URI: ' .. uri)
            dispatchers.notification('textDocument/publishDiagnostics', {
              uri = uri,
              diagnostics = {{
                range = {
                  start = { line = 0, character = 0 },
                  ['end'] = { line = 0, character = 1 },
                },
                severity = 1,
                message = 'Diagnostic for the opened document',
              }},
            })
          end)
        end
        return true
      end,
      is_closing = function() return closing end,
      terminate = function() closing = true end,
    }
  end,
})
assert(client_id, 'LSP client did not start')

vim.defer_fn(function()
  local diagnostics = vim.diagnostic.get()
  local target = diagnostics[1] and diagnostics[1].bufnr
  print(vim.inspect({
    original_buffer = original,
    second_buffer = second,
    original_uri = vim.uri_from_bufnr(original),
    second_uri = vim.uri_from_bufnr(second),
    diagnostics_on_original = #vim.diagnostic.get(original),
    total_diagnostics = #diagnostics,
    diagnostic_buffer = target,
    diagnostic_buffer_name = target and vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(target),
  }))
  local client = vim.lsp.get_client_by_id(client_id)
  if client then client:stop(true) end
  vim.cmd('qa!')
end, 500)
```

Actual output on the official nightly:

```text
didOpen URI: file://
{
  diagnostic_buffer = 3,
  diagnostic_buffer_name = "/",
  diagnostics_on_original = 0,
  original_buffer = 1,
  original_uri = "file://",
  second_buffer = 2,
  second_uri = "file://",
  total_diagnostics = 1
}
```

The same issue reproduces on v0.12.6.

Two control cases pass on both versions:

- Giving the original buffer a filename before starting the client results in `diagnostics_on_original = 1`, with the diagnostic assigned to that original buffer. The file does not need to exist on disk.
- A local workaround that assigns each unnamed buffer a unique synthetic URI and maps it back to the original buffer also results in `diagnostics_on_original = 1`. This workaround is only evidence that the URI mapping is responsible, not a proposed upstream implementation.

### Expected behavior

An unnamed `[No Name]` buffer should be able to receive and display LSP diagnostics without first having to be named or saved, when the language server supports the document and returns diagnostics for it. Diagnostics should be associated with the original buffer, and different unnamed buffers should have distinct document identities so their diagnostics remain separate.

### Nvim version (`nvim -v`)

- Official nightly: `NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1943+gd714648b8e` (downloaded 2026-10-23)
- Also reproduced: `NVIM v0.12.6`

### Language server name/version

Self-contained in-process test server included above (`unnamed-diagnostic-repro`).

### Operating system/version

NixOS 26.05 (Yarara), Linux x86_64.

### Log file

The reproduction prints the received `didOpen` URI and the resulting diagnostic buffer/counts; output is included above.

### Related discussion and implementation

Related: #21276 discusses URI schemes for in-memory documents. This report provides a concrete reproduction of diagnostics being routed to the wrong buffer; it does not require any particular URI scheme as the solution.

Relevant code at the tested nightly commit:

- [`uri_from_bufnr()` / `uri_to_fname()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/d714648b8e7c476b7b5c1f661aa192b179bfc1d3/runtime/lua/vim/uri.lua)
- [`handle_diagnostics()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/d714648b8e7c476b7b5c1f661aa192b179bfc1d3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/diagnostic.lua), which converts the URI to a filename and calls `bufadd()`.

Ultimately, I would like LSP diagnostics to work in unnamed buffers as well, so I can edit temporary code and see its diagnostics before choosing a filename or saving it.

title: LSP: diagnostics for unnamed buffers are assigned to the wrong buffer (shared file:// URI)
